common_patterns.overview: Reusable fixes for the defects this mode reports most often. Use these as the shape of the improved code. Adapt names to the file under review. Every sample keeps the original behaviour unless the pattern note says otherwise. Samples are in C#, the language of this repository. The ideas are language-neutral.

pattern.name: guard_clauses
pattern.symptom: Deep nesting hides the normal path. The failure path needs a hunt to find.
pattern.fix: Reject each invalid case at the top. Leave the normal path flat and last.
pattern.note: Same behaviour, same side effects. Only the reading cost drops.

pattern.name: validator_with_positive_test
pattern.symptom: A new rejection branch is added with no test that reaches it.
pattern.fix: Ship the validator and the test that feeds it bad input, in the same change.
pattern.note: An untested rejection path is assumed broken until proven otherwise.

pattern.name: try_pattern
pattern.symptom: Expected absence is signalled by throwing and catching an exception.
pattern.fix: Use a Try method that returns a boolean and an out value. Keep exceptions for the unexpected.
pattern.after:
if (!TryGetSheet(workbook, "Config", out var sheet)) return;
Use(sheet);
pattern.note: Also removes the catch-all that was hiding every other failure.

pattern.name: empty_collection_contract
pattern.symptom: A method returns null sometimes and a list other times. Callers all guard differently.
pattern.fix: Return an empty collection. State it in the name or the doc comment. Drop the null guards.
pattern.note: Callers can now loop without a null check. One contract, not many guesses.

pattern.name: explicit_result_over_magic_value
pattern.symptom: Failure is signalled by -1, an empty string, or a null that also means "not found".
pattern.fix: Return a small result type that carries success, the value, and the reason.
pattern.before: int index = FindLane("Design"); // -1 means missing if (index >= 0) { ... }
pattern.note: Use this when the reason matters. For pure presence checks the Try pattern is smaller.

pattern.name: extract_method_mixed_responsibility
pattern.symptom: One method validates, computes, formats, and writes. Changing the format risks the validation.
pattern.fix: Extract by reason to change. Keep the original method as a short sequence of named steps.
pattern.note: Do not extract a method for a single call site with no separate reason to change.

pattern.name: split_flag_parameter
pattern.symptom: A boolean parameter switches the whole behaviour of a method or constructor.
pattern.fix: Split into two named operations, or make the caller state the choice in a named type.
pattern.before: Draw(row, true); // what does true mean here?
pattern.note: If both cases really share the body, keep one method and pass a named enum instead.

pattern.name: deterministic_clock_and_culture
pattern.symptom: The result depends on today's date, the machine culture, or dictionary order.
pattern.fix: Pass the time and the culture in. Order collections explicitly.
pattern.before: var label = DateTime.Now.ToString("d"); var first = lookup.Values.First();
pattern.after: var label = clock.Today.ToString("d", culture); var first = lookup.Values.OrderBy(v => v.Key, StringComparer.Ordinal).First();
pattern.note: Tests can now pin the date and the culture. The output stops moving between machines.

pattern.name: resource_ownership
pattern.symptom: A handle, stream, or COM object is created and released only on the happy path.
pattern.fix: Own it in one place. Release it on every exit path.
pattern.after: using var stream = File.OpenWrite(path); WritePng(stream, image);
pattern.note: If the object is not disposable, wrap it in one tested helper and call that helper once.

pattern.name: single_enumeration
pattern.symptom: A lazy sequence is walked more than once. The second walk recomputes or re-queries.
pattern.fix: Materialise once, then reuse the list.
pattern.before: if (rows.Any()) { foreach (var row in rows) Draw(row); }
pattern.note: Watch for this in loops and in logging. Count and iteration are two walks.

pattern.name: all_or_nothing_update
pattern.symptom: A partial failure leaves half the state changed and no way back.
pattern.fix: Build the full result first. Apply it in one step. Roll back if the step fails.
pattern.before: foreach (var row in rows) { DeleteShapes(row); DrawRow(row); }
pattern.note: This is the shape to ask for when the review finds a half-rendered chart.

pattern.name: fire_and_forget_async
pattern.symptom: A task is started and never awaited. Failures vanish. Ordering is lost.
pattern.fix: Await it, or keep the task and observe it on a named path.
pattern.note: If the caller cannot await, say so in the finding. Do not hide the failure.
